title: August's Full Moon Will Turn Blood Red During a Stunning Eclipse!
summary: Get ready for a sky show! On August 28, the full moon will put on a special performance — it will turn a deep, reddish color during a lunar eclipse. This happens when Earth moves right between the sun and the moon, casting a shadow that makes the moon look like it's blushing. This month's full moon is called the Sturgeon Moon. Native American tribes named it after the giant sturgeon fish that were easiest to catch in the Great Lakes around this time. But you might also hear it called the Flying Up Moon (when young birds first fly) or the Corn Moon. The eclipse will be visible across the Americas, parts of Europe, and Africa. In the U.S., the moon rises at sunset on August 27. At first, it might look yellow-orange near the horizon — that's because Earth's atmosphere scatters blue light, leaving the warmer colors. It might also seem bigger than usual thanks to the "Moon Illusion," a trick your brain plays when the moon is near trees or buildings. As the night goes on, Earth's shadow will slowly creep across the moon. At the peak, up to 96% of the moon will be covered! Only a thin sliver will stay bright. The shadowed part will glow a gorgeous blood red, caused by sunlight filtering through Earth's atmosphere — the same reason sunsets look red. Don't forget to look around the moon, too. You'll spot the Summer Triangle — three bright stars: Vega, Altair, and Deneb. And if you look west, you might catch Venus shining low on the horizon. The eclipse starts late on August 27 for most viewers, so you might need to stay up late. But it's totally worth it!
why_it_matters: Watching the sky helps you feel connected to nature and gives you a chance to see Earth's shadow in action, just like you learn about in science class.

background_read: Lunar eclipses happen only during a full moon, when the Earth lines up directly between the sun and moon.
Many cultures around the world named full moons based on seasonal changes, like the Sturgeon Moon when fishing was best.
The Moon Illusion has fascinated people for centuries—even though the moon doesn't really change size, our brains can't help but see it as bigger near the ground.
Article_Structure: WHO: The Moon, Earth, and Sun, with Native American tribes who named the Sturgeon Moon.
WHAT: A deep lunar eclipse will turn almost all of the moon a blood-red color visible across continents.
WHERE: Visible in the Americas, parts of Europe, and Africa.
WHY: Because Earth's shadow blocks direct sunlight, but red light still reaches the moon after filtering through our atmosphere.

perspectives.description: This eclipse is a beautiful, free show that you can watch with your family without needing any special equipment, just your eyes.
For many kids, staying up late to see the eclipse might be tough, but photos and videos will be shared so you can see it the next day if you miss it.
It's a reminder that the same forces that make sunsets red also paint the moon, linking sky and Earth in a beautiful demonstration of light.
